issue_context.title: Debugger incorrectly resolves argument in MethodImplOptions.NoOptimization frame in Windows x86
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description

The VS Debugger attempts to scraps the 'tasks' array from the [System.Private.CoreLib.dll!System.Threading.Tasks.Task.WaitAll(System.Threading.Tasks.Task[] tasks)](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/8ddb6335236416562dca5e00eddc812d1d0f3340/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Threading/Tasks/Task.cs#L4591) frame of the call stack in order to understand wait relationships. This method is marked with `MethodImplOptions.NoOptimization` in order to make this possible. But something changed in either preview 5 or preview 6 so that this no longer works in x86 Windows.

### Configuration

* Which version of .NET is the code running on? 6.0 preview 7
* What OS and version, and what distro if applicable? Windows 10
* What is the architecture (x64, x86, ARM, ARM64)? x86
* Do you know whether it is specific to that configuration? Yes

### Regression?

Yes

### Other information

This issue reproduces both with live debugging and a dump. I have a dump available if any Microsoft employee would like it.

From the dump, here is the stack memory for the WaitAll frame:

| VFrame relative address | Address | Value | Notes |
| -------------------------- | --------- | ------ | ------ |
| $vframe-16 | 0x02FBEF78 | 7b5ce584 | Where ICorDebug tells us `args` is |
| $vframe-12  | 0x02FBEF7C | 00000000 | |
| $vframe-8 | 0x02FBEF80 | 00000000 | |
| $vframe-4 | 0x02FBEF84 | 05550778 | Where `args` actually is |
| $vframe | 0x02FBEF88 | 02fbefa8 | Saved EBP |
| $vframe+4 | 0x02FBEF8C | 08992e81 | Return address |

Disassembly:
```
        public static void WaitAll(params Task[] tasks)
        {
            WaitAllCore(tasks, Timeout.Infinite, default);
7B5CE560  push        ebp  
7B5CE561  mov         ebp,esp  
7B5CE563  sub         esp,8  
7B5CE566  xor         eax,eax  
7B5CE568  mov         dword ptr [ebp-8],eax  
7B5CE56B  mov         dword ptr [ebp-4],ecx  <- Storing args in [$vframe - 4]
7B5CE56E  xor         ecx,ecx  
7B5CE570  mov         dword ptr [ebp-8],ecx  
7B5CE573  push        dword ptr [ebp-8]  
7B5CE576  mov         ecx,dword ptr [ebp-4]  
7B5CE579  mov         edx,0FFFFFFFFh  
7B5CE57E  call        dword ptr [Pointer to: CLRStub[MethodCallThunk]@92b7b12c7b7a3d20 (7BC53DDCh)]  
7B5CE584  mov         esp,ebp  
7B5CE586  pop         ebp  
7B5CE587  ret  
```

### Repro steps

1. Create a new .NET 6 console project.
2. Open the project file and add `<RuntimeIdentifier>win7-x86</RuntimeIdentifier>`
3. Add the following source code
4. Launch the project under the debugger
5. After the program is running Debug->Break
6. Switch to the Task.WaitAll frame
7. Switch to the locals window and attempt to evaluate `tasks`

Result:
| Name | Value | Type |
| -- | -- | -- |
| tasks | Unable to read memory | System.Threading.Tasks.Task[] |

```C#
class Program
{
    static private async Task<int> SlowNumber()
    {
        // Wait for 20 seconds.
        await Task.Delay(20000);
        return 12;
    }

    public static void Main(string[] args)
    {
        Task t1 = SlowNumber();
        Task t2 = SlowNumber();
        Task.WaitAll(t1, t2);
    }
}
```

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/0767243f100777704ffd7f426d372acdeaa28362/src/coreclr/tools/aot/ILCompiler.Reflection.ReadyToRun/DebugInfo.cs#L221-L230

cc @trylek
I agree it looks weird. I must admit I have no recollection of coding this up whatsoever, @davidwrighton, do you happen to remember why this was put there in the first place?
Git blame says it came from the original PR to add debug info support: https://github.com/dotnet/coreclr/pull/19870.

That code is weird, but not wrong. There is an assumption that on X86 locals are DWORD aligned, and so we compress the debug info a bit on x86. I'll work up the logic to compress the data on X86 and see if we can get it into RC1.

review_comments: Nit - if at some point we considered expanding this behavior to other architectures, the name of the argument (assume4ByteAligned) would probably need to change to e.g. something like encodeUsingPointerSizeUnits or some such. If we believe this to be limited to X86 forever, it's probably OK.

I just checked to see how valuable this really is, and we could save something like 0.08% of System.Private.CoreLib.dll size if we applied a similar size optimization on X64. I don't see that as worthwhile given the complexity it would impose on the reader in the runtime.
`TargetDetails` are available in `_method.Context.Target`. The additional parameter caused an unnecessary NativeAOT build break.
